'''Mariano Díaz''' '''Mejía''' (Spanish pronunciation: [[Help:IPA/Spanish|[maˈɾjano ˈði.aθ meˈxi.a]]]; born 1 August 1993), better known as '''Mariano''', is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Spanish football updater|Alavés}} club [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]]. Born in Spain, he plays for the [[Dominican Republic national football team|Dominican Republic national team]].

Shortly after making his debut for [[CF Badalona|Badalona]] in 2011, Mariano joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], where he played in the [[Real Madrid C|C-team]] and then the [[Real Madrid Castilla|reserves]], where he was top scorer in the [[2015–16 Segunda División B]]. He then began playing with the first team, and was part of their squad that won [[La Liga]], the [[UEFA Champions League]] and the [[FIFA Club World Cup]] in 2016–17. He was subsequently signed by [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Premià de Mar]], [[Province of Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Catalonia]], Mariano began his youth career with local side [[RCD Espanyol]], and appeared for lowly [[CE Premià]] and Fundació Sánchez Llibre. In 2009, he joined [[CF Badalona]], and made his senior debut on 21 August 2011, replacing [[Iñaki Goikoetxea]] for the final 21 minutes of a 1–0 loss at [[CD Teruel]] in the [[Segunda División B]] [[2011–12 Segunda División B|season]]; he made two more appearances off the bench. On the 31st, he made his first start, playing the entirety of a 3–1 loss at [[RB Linense]] in [[2011–12 Copa del Rey|that season]]'s [[Copa del Rey]], scoring his team's consolation.<ref>{{cite news|title=El Badalona se convierte en la tercera víctima de la todopoderosa Balona|trans-title=Badalona become the third victim of the almighty ''Balona''|url=http://www.lalineadigital.es/2011/09/3-1-el-badalona-se-convierte-en-la-tercera-victima-de-la-todopoderosa-balona/|access-date=16 March 2016|publisher=La Línea Digital|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321163319/http://www.lalineadigital.es/2011/09/3-1-el-badalona-se-convierte-en-la-tercera-victima-de-la-todopoderosa-balona/|archive-date=21 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
====Youth and Castilla====
Shortly after, Mariano signed with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], returning to youth football.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Martín|first1=Iván|title=Mariano, el hombre gol de Zidane|trans-title=Mariano, Zidane's goal man|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/10/27/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1445933346.html|access-date=16 March 2016|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=27 October 2015|language=es}}</ref> In August 2012 he was promoted to the [[Madrid|Madrilenian]] side's [[Real Madrid C|C-team]] also in the third level. He became a regular in his [[2013–14 Segunda División B|second season there]], scoring 15 goals in 26 matches, including a [[hat-trick]] on 22 December 2013 in a 5–2 home win over [[Sestao River Club]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vázquez|first1=Javi|title=Goleada ante el Sestao River para terminar el año|trans-title=Thrashing of Sestao River to finish the year|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/noticias/2013/12/5-2-goleada-ante-el-sestao-river-para-terminar-el-ano|access-date=16 March 2016|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=22 December 2013|language=es}}</ref> The following 18 January, Mariano made his professional debut at the [[Estadio Alfredo Di Stéfano]], appearing with [[Real Madrid Castilla|the reserves]] in a 1–2 loss against [[Sporting de Gijón]] in the [[Segunda División]]; he came on for the final five minutes in place of [[Raúl de Tomás]].<ref>[http://www.marca.com/2014/01/18/futbol/2adivision/1390071555.html Los rojiblancos meten máxima presión al Deportivo (''Rojiblancos'' puts maximum pressure on Deportivo)]; ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'', 18 January 2014 {{in lang|es}}</ref>

In [[2014–15 Segunda División B|2014–15]], with Castilla now in the third tier, Mariano was indefinitely promoted to the team. He made ten appearances, six from the bench, and scored five times. On 29 March, he entered late in De Tomás' place again and scored twice to cap a 5–1 home win over [[UD Las Palmas B]],<ref>{{cite news |last=Jiménez|first=Bárbara|title=5–1: Castilla claim big win at the Di Stéfano|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/03/5-1-castilla-claim-big-win-at-the-di-stefano|access-date=16 March 2016|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=29 March 2015}}</ref> while one week later, he was given a start at lowly [[UB Conquense]] and struck both goals in a seven-minute span.<ref>{{cite news|title=Un doblete de Mariano lanza al Castilla frente al colista|trans-title=Mariano's brace is the springboard for Castilla against the bottom team|url=http://as.com/videos/2015/04/05/portada/1428262401_072936.html|access-date=16 March 2016|publisher=Diario AS|date=5 April 2015|language=es|archive-date=20 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160320080218/http://as.com/videos/2015/04/05/portada/1428262401_072936.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 24 October 2015, Mariano scored all of his team's goals in a 3–1 home win over [[UD Socuéllamos]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Hat-trick del dominicano Mariano con el Castilla|trans-title=Hat-trick for the Dominican Mariano with Castilla |url=http://www.marca.com/2015/10/24/futbol/futbol_internacional/resto_de_america/1445712135.html|access-date=24 October 2015|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=24 October 2015|language=es}}</ref> and repeated this on 8 November in a 3–2 win against [[CF Fuenlabrada]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Martín|first1=Iván|title=El Castilla baila al ritmo de Mariano|trans-title=Castilla dance to Mariano's rhythm|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/11/08/futbol/mas_futbol/1447010594.html|access-date=16 March 2016|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=8 November 2013|language=es}}</ref> The following 17 April, he scored his third treble of the season, scoring all of the goals – two penalties – in a home win over [[SD Gernika Club]] which put Castilla top.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Forjanes|first1=Carlos|title=Mariano hat-trick fires Real Madrid Castilla top|url=http://en.as.com/en/2016/04/18/football/1460979613_949666.html|access-date=18 April 2016|publisher=Diario AS|date=18 April 2016|archive-date=4 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304123139/https://en.as.com/en/2016/04/18/football/1460979613_949666.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored his 25th goal of the season in a 6–1 win over [[La Roda CF]] on the last day of the season, making him the season's top scorer and winning the group at the expense of [[Barakaldo CF]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vargas|first1=Diego|title=Goleada de campeonato del Castilla a La Roda|trans-title=Castilla's championship thrashing of La Roda|url=http://www.defensacentral.com/la_fabrica/1463327881-goleada-de-campeonato-del-castilla-a-la-roda|access-date=16 May 2016|publisher=Defensa Central|date=15 May 2016|language=es}}</ref>

====2016–17: Entrance in the first squad====
Mariano was definitively promoted to the main squad by manager [[Zinedine Zidane]] on 20 August 2016, after a back injury to striker [[Karim Benzema]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2016/08/20/57b8456fe5fdead1488b4575.html|title=Mariano se queda en la primera plantilla del Madrid|trans-title=Mariano stays in Real Madrid's first team|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=20 August 2016|access-date=20 August 2016}}</ref> One week later, Mariano made his senior debut during a 2–1 win over [[Celta de Vigo]], replacing [[Álvaro Morata]] in the 77th minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37179134 |title=Real Madrid 2–1 Celta Vigo|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 August 2016|access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> On 26 October, again from the bench, he scored his first goal for the ''Merengues'' to conclude a 7–1 win at [[Cultural y Deportiva Leonesa]] in the [[Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Asensio, Morata star as Real Madrid score seven in Copa del Rey rout|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/report?gameId=467684|access-date=27 October 2016|publisher=ESPN|date=26 October 2016}}</ref> In the second leg, he added a hat-trick for a 13–2 aggregate win, including a 23rd-second goal that was his team's fastest goal in the competition.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mariano scores Real Madrid's fastest ever Copa del Rey goal|url=http://en.as.com/en/2016/11/30/football/1480537991_088399.html|access-date=17 December 2016|work=Diario AS|date=30 November 2016|archive-date=3 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201203022001/https://en.as.com/en/2016/11/30/football/1480537991_088399.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Mariano scored his first top-flight goal on 10 December, equalising in a 3–2 comeback victory at home to [[Deportivo de La Coruña]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mariano Díaz marcó un gol en la victoria del Real Madrid sobre Deportivo|trans-title=Mariano Díaz scored a goal in Real Madrid's victory over Deportivo|url=http://www.diariolibre.com/deportes/futbol/mariano-diaz-marco-un-gol-en-la-victoria-del-real-madrid-sobre-deportivo-CE5699765 |access-date=17 December 2016|work=Diario Libre|date=10 December 2016|language=es}}</ref> Later that month, he was part of the squad that won the [[2016 FIFA Club World Cup]] in Japan, but did not appear in either of Real Madrid's matches.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=276110/match=300364982/match-report.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161216162358/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=276110/match=300364982/match-report.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=16 December 2016 |title=Real overcome America to reach final |access-date=11 March 2017|publisher=FIFA|date=15 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Madrid see off spirited Kashima in electric extra time final|url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=276112/match=300364984/match-report.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220125922/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=276112/match=300364984/match-report.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 December 2016|access-date=11 March 2017|publisher=FIFA|date=18 December 2016}}</ref> Mariano made eight appearances when Madrid won the [[2016–17 La Liga]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|date=21 May 2017 |work=La Liga}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Real Madrid win La Liga title with victory at Malaga|date=21 May 2017 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> He was a back-up when Madrid won the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|date=3 June 2017|publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

===Lyon===
On 30 June 2017, Mariano signed for [[Olympique Lyonnais]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/06/official-announcement-mariano|title=Official Announcement: Mariano|date=30 June 2017|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olweb.fr/fr/article/mercato-a-la-decouverte-de-la-nouvelle-recrue-mariano-diaz-31369.html|title=Mercato : A la découverte de la nouvelle recrue Mariano Diaz|date=30 June 2017|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|trans-title=Transfer market: Meet new recruit Mariano Díaz}}</ref> The fee was reported as €8&nbsp;million plus 35% interest on the capital gain of a potential future transfer.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mariano presented at Lyon, leaves Real Madrid for €8&nbsp;million|url=https://en.as.com/en/2017/06/30/football/1498838723_955213.html|access-date=14 September 2017|work=Diario AS|date=30 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fullmatchesandshows.com/2017/10/20/lyon-deny-real-madrid-buy-back-clause-for-mariano-diaz/|title=Lyon deny Real Madrid buy-back clause for Mariano Diaz|access-date=23 October 2017|archive-date=27 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627154825/https://www.fullmatchesandshows.com/2017/10/20/lyon-deny-real-madrid-buy-back-clause-for-mariano-diaz/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut on 5 August in the first match of the [[2017–18 Ligue 1]] season against [[RC Strasbourg Alsace]], scoring twice in a 4–0 home win.<ref>{{cite news|title=OL-STRASBOURG: WITH FEKIR AND MARIANO STEPPING UP, OL ARE ALREADY ON THE ATTACK! (4–0)|url=http://www.olweb.fr/en/article/ol-strasbourg-with-fekir-and-mariano-up-front-ol-are-already-on-the-attack-4-0-31703.html|access-date=14 September 2017|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|date=5 August 2017}}</ref> He totalled 18 goals for the league season, forming a prolific attacking trio alongside [[Memphis Depay]] and [[Nabil Fekir]] (19 and 18 goals respectively).<ref>{{cite news |title=Ligue 1 : le classement des buteurs de la saison 2017–2018 |trans-title=Ligue 1: top scorers of the 2017–2018 season|url=http://www.europe1.fr/sport/ligue-1-le-classement-des-buteurs-de-la-saison-2017-2018-3657113 |access-date=31 August 2018 |publisher=Europe 1 |date=19 May 2018 |language=fr}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid===
On 29 August 2018, Real Madrid announced they had signed Mariano on a five-year contract. As the Spanish club already owned 35% of his playing rights, the fee was reduced to €23&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Mariano|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/official-announcement-mariano|access-date=29 August 2018|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=29 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=OL agree transfer of Mariano Diaz to Real Madrid|url=https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/articles/2018/08/29/ol-agree-transfer-of-mariano-diaz-to-real-madrid|access-date=29 August 2018|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|date=29 August 2018}}</ref> He was given the number 7 shirt, previously worn by [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.the42.ie/mariano-diaz-real-madrid-signing-number-seven-shirt-4213181-Aug2018/|title=Real Madrid's new signing handed number 7 shirt after €33m move from Lyon|last=Team|first=The42|work=The42|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid/story/3618322/real-madrids-mariano-diaz-takes-cristiano-ronaldos-no-7-shirt-is-with-you|title=Real Madrid give Ronaldo's No. 7 shirt to Mariano|publisher=ESPN|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref> His second debut was on 19 September, coming on as a 73rd-minute substitute against [[A.S. Roma]] in the first fixture of the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League]] group stage, and he scored the last goal of a 3–0 victory with a curved shot from outside the [[penalty area]].<ref>{{cite news|title=MATCH SUMMARY: Real Madrid 3–0 Roma|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2025065--real-madrid-vs-roma/|access-date=20 September 2018|publisher=UEFA|date=19 September 2018}}</ref> On 1 March 2020, having just came off the bench for his first league appearance of the season, he scored with his first touch of the ball in the 90th minute of a 2–0 [[El Clásico]] victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/us/el-clasico/video/mariano-doubles-real-madrids-lead-over-barca/1425076|title=Mariano Doubles Real Madrid's Lead Over Barca in El Clasico|website=BeIN Sports|access-date=2 March 2020}}</ref> He made five appearances during the league season, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|website=Marca}}</ref> In July 2020, Mariano tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/28/mariano-medical-report|title=Mariano medical report|date=28 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|access-date=28 July 2020}}</ref>

On 3 June 2023, Real Madrid announced that Mariano would leave the club at the expiration of his contract on 30 June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Official Statement: Mariano|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/06/03/official-statement-mariano|access-date=3 June 2023 |website=Real Madrid}}</ref>

===Sevilla===
On 1 September 2023, Mariano signed for fellow La Liga club [[Sevilla FC]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Agreement in principle for the signing of Mariano Díaz |url=https://sevillafc.es/en/actual/news/agreement-principle-mariano-diaz |publisher=[[Sevilla FC]] |access-date=1 September 2023 |date=1 September 2023 |archive-date=6 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230906225003/https://sevillafc.es/en/actual/news/agreement-principle-mariano-diaz |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Espina |first=José A. |date=1 September 2023 |title=Oficial: ¡Mariano, la bomba del Sevilla! |url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/mariano-la-bomba-del-sevilla-n/ |access-date=2 September 2023 |website=Diario AS |language=es}}</ref>

===Alavés===
In July 2025, after more than a year as a [[free agent]], Mariano joined [[Deportivo Alavés]] on trial.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/deportes/orgullodenervion/noticias-sevilla-fc/mariano-diaz-sevilla-prueba-deportivo-alaves-20250714135429-nts.html|title=Mariano Díaz, ex del Sevilla FC, a prueba con el Deportivo Alavés|trans-title=Mariano Díaz, formerly of Sevilla FC, on trial at Deportivo Alavés|publisher=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|language=es|date=14 July 2025|accessdate=7 August 2025}}</ref> On 7 August, after playing in the pre-season, he signed a two-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deportivoalaves.com/es/noticias/mariano-diaz-refuerza-el-ataque-del-glorioso|title=Mariano Díaz refuerza el ataque del Glorioso|trans-title=Mariano Díaz bolsters the attack of the ''Glorioso''|publisher=Deportivo Alavés|language=es|date=7 August 2025|accessdate=7 August 2025}}</ref>

On 15 August 2026, Mariano scored his first league goal for Alavés (and his first in 5 seasons) in their opening game of the season against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] with a superb finish into the top right corner. He also assisted the other 2 goals in a dominant 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/laliga-sevilla-rayo-vallecano-getafe-alaves-47b39787bbb5397463b20fd9c10db464|title=Mariano Díaz thrives and Alaves beats 10-man Getafe 3-0 as La Liga kicks off Europe’s domestic league season|website=[[Associated Press|AP News]]}}</ref>

==International career==
Mariano is eligible for the [[Dominican Republic national football team|Dominican Republic]] through his mother, a native of [[San Juan de la Maguana]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mariano Díaz: el dominicano promovido al Real Madrid|trans-title=Mariano Díaz: the Dominican promoted to Real Madrid|url=http://www.metrord.do/deportes/mariano-diaz-el-dominicano-promovido-al-real-madrid/ftwpbs---CDvNvWrc1rK2Y/|access-date=23 May 2016|publisher=Metro RD|date=18 February 2016|language=es}}</ref> He made his international debut on 24 March 2013 in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against neighbours [[Haiti national football team|Haiti]], and scored the last goal of a 3–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mariano, from Madrid to the Caribbean|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/03/27/en/football/real_madrid/1364368925.html|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=27 March 2013|access-date=5 February 2014}}</ref> He later retired from the national team to focus on his career at Real Madrid and also to avoid being [[cap-tied]] with the Dominican Republic, in view of a possible call up for the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]].<ref name=fichajes>{{cite web|url=http://www.fichajes.net/noticias/mariano-jugar-espana-20160824.html|title=Mariano puede jugar con España|language=es|trans-title=Mariano can play with Spain|publisher=Fichajes.net|first=Héctor|last=Andreu|date=24 August 2016|access-date=22 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://madrid-barcelona.com/2016-08-24/mariano-diaz-puede-jugar-la-seleccion-espanola/|title=Mariano Díaz puede jugar con la Selección española|language=es|trans-title=Mariano Díaz can play with the Spanish national team|date=24 August 2016|access-date=22 December 2016}}</ref> In December 2017, Spain manager [[Julen Lopetegui]] said he was monitoring Mariano for a call-up.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gabilondo |first1=Aritz |title=Lopetegui: "A Mariano ya fuimos a verle; le seguimos de cerca" |trans-title=Lopetegui "We already went to see Mariano; we are following him closely|url=https://as.com/futbol/2017/12/30/seleccion/1514660182_590260.html |access-date=31 August 2018 |date=31 December 2017 |language=es}}</ref> In March 2025, he was called up to the Dominican Republic national team after 303 days without playing a club match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/futbol-internacional/2025/03/23/mariano-reporta-listo-republica-dominicana-volvera-jugar-despues-303-dias.html|title=Mariano se reporta listo con República Dominicana y volverá a jugar... ¡Después de 303 días!|first=SERGIO|last=RIVERA|date=23 March 2025|website=MARCA}}</ref>
